selection.method: hard gate (0 collisions AND mission_complete) first, then composite/tie-break only among gate-passers
selection.fw_sweep: baseline passes hard gate cleanly; policy fails (mission_timeout, incomplete) -> baseline wins
selection.fw_replan (Wall Went Up): NEITHER approach clears the hard gate — baseline completed but incurred 1 collision (fails on collision alone, per plan's 'a crash scores 0' rule); policy neither completed nor collision-free (stall+timeout). Honest result, not massaged: matches the plan's own risk note that the early policy_fw.onnx may fail hard gates, but shows the reactive baseline is ALSO not yet a clean pass on this scenario — replan/reroute-around-a-new-obstacle is not yet solved by either approach at hard-gate standard.
selection.overall: reactive baseline is the current best of the 2 measurable approaches (1/2 scenarios hard-gate-clean vs 0/2 for the learned policy); VLM-reasoning approach untested pending real hardware

godot_capability_metrics.note: Perception/memory/explore capabilities can't be scored by scorecard.py (fleet Mission 'finds' targets by bare proximity, no vision/occlusion) — measured instead via fw_eval.py's Godot capability harness, which drives the REAL production backends.SimBackend/spatial_memory.SpatialMemory/search_patterns code with a scripted flight profile (not the reactive_goto_controller used above, and not a stand-in for VLM judgment — see fw_eval.py's own docstring).
